reviews.text: I wish I could explain how much I love this place such a great people who genuinely take care of your fur babies. Happy to have gone here. 20/10

The vets are genuinely kind and gentle with animals, but unfortunately, they did not tell me how serious my cat’s declining condition had become, and they did not identify an abdominal mass on her until it was too late.

I followed all Drs recommendations and spent thousands of dollars on the exams, treatments, X-rays, ultrasounds, and medications they suggested. Despite all of this, her health continued to decline.
She was losing weight, losing her appetite and feeling unwell. I had concerns about changes in her behaviour, including urinating outside the litter box, but the doctor was unable to give me an answer. (I was later told at the emergency hospital that this may have been related to something putting pressure on her bladder).
I felt that some of her symptoms were brushed off or were being treated individually rather than looking closely at what the underlying cause could be. Eventually the doctor told me he did not know why she was becoming so sick and referred me to a specialist. However, the appointment was several weeks away and by that point my cat could barely hold herself up. I knew I could not wait any longer so I took her to an emergency animal hospital shortly after, where I was absolutely devastated by what I was told.
The doctors at the emergency hospital told me that my cat was in a very serious state, was severely dehydrated, and had an abdominal mass. I cannot understand how the severity of her condition and the abdominal mass were not identified sooner, especially since she had been seen at this clinic only a few DAYS earlier and numerous times throughout the year!!

Unfortunately, my beloved cat passed away shortly afterward, and I am completely heartbroken and devastated. I will always wonder if more could have been done if her declining health had been taken more seriously and investigated more thoroughly.
I understand that veterinarians cannot always know immediately what is wrong, and I do not expect a doctor to have every answer immediately. But they should be able to identify a mass on an animal and inform pet owners of the seriousness of the pet's health. If the vets don't know, then the owner should be informed and advised to seek a second opinion or specialized care immediately, before it's too late.
YOU GUYS ARE THE BEST!!!

I’m sorry that I put my own cat through months of unnecessary stress and suffering by bringing her to this clinic.
I brought my cat here for several months because of chronic diarrhea. Even after months of visits, they had still not done basic bloodwork. Instead, it felt like the focus was on charging as much as possible while repeatedly putting my cat through unnecessary treatments and stress.
There was also a serious lack of communication between the doctors. Every time we saw a different veterinarian, we were given different recommendations, without any clear communication or coordination between them.
I regret choosing this clinic simply because I didn’t have enough experience to know what to expect from a veterinary clinic. After I finally switched to another veterinarian, my cat’s problem was resolved with a simple approach and bloodwork.
I wish I had gone somewhere else from the beginning. My experience was extremely disappointing, and I felt that there was very little accountability or continuity of care for my pet

Beware & be cautious.  The first priority at this clinic is $$$. I brought my cat here as she had very bad teeth and needed medical attention. One of the very first things I told the vet and the assistant in the initial consultation is that she could not have chicken and please do not feed her chicken. What did they do? Fed her chicken for the entire time she was in their care.  One of the vets told me that she had no issues with chicken which is blatantly untrue. My question is this:  Who knew this cat better? Someone who had seen her for a few hours or someone who looked after her daily for 12 years?
I will admit that in the beginning I felt I had hit the jackpot here. Everyone seemed very caring and wanting the best for the animal. After a couple of days, I had doubts and I had questions. Money was front & centre all the time.  After the surgery for the teeth, she was in such rough shape that she had to be force-fed and they expected me to do that at home. I returned her to the clinic where she was force-fed and stayed one more night.   The vet then expected me to take her home at night, bring her back in the mornings to be force-fed until she started eating on her own.  She was in great pain and her stress level was over the moon.  One explanation the vet offered was that she was stressed because of the carrier crate.  If that was the case, why would he expect me to put her in it twice a day  to be brought back to the clinic until she could eat on her own.  Again, the poor girl's pain & stress was beyond measure & contributed to the agonizing decision that was made.  Long story short, after $7,000+, I decided to put her down and put her out of her misery.  The euthanasia cost another $1,100+.  I'm sure they will try to justify anything and everything. That's fine, they can say what they want but what I know is that the very very last thing I expected was to have to make the heart-breaking and gut-wrenching decision to put my girl down.  I will again say:  who knew her better?  Someone who spent a couple of days with her or a few hours or someone who looked after her for 12 years.
Just be cautious and ask lots of questions and, most importantly, ensure that they follow your instructions rather than ignoring them.
Thankfully, my sister attended each time with me & saw my girl going downhill and heard everything that was said.  I am thankful to have a witness.

Avoid this hospital. They are more concerned with prescribing medications and pushing unnecessary tests rather than listening to pet owners who know and understand their pets and their pets’ needs. We came in with an injured ankle exacerbated by a chronic condition. The vet insisted that my dog had a luxating hip even though there was no indication of this and the symptoms were localized to his ankle. The vet insisted that an xray of the entire leg and hip was necessary despite me questioning the necessity of a hip xray. The vet tech could not properly explain the risks of sedation on an 11 year old dog which made me doubt the safety of my dog. Bloodwork was also not done before sedation. Once the X-rays were completed, it was confirmed that there was nothing wrong with his hip just as I had said. That testing was entirely unnecessary and instead caused stress to my dog. The vet did not appear to have the skills to properly interpret the X-ray as he kept suggesting my dog had bone cancer despite no previous indication of cancer. The vet continued to ignore my explanation that my dog had a chronic 9-year old injury on the very same spot which likely explained his symptoms. Instead, the vet appeared more concerned about pushing a radiologist interpretation of the X-rays and recommending further testing. One of the medications prescribed to my dog was entirely inappropriate for the injury sustained. The radiologist report confirmed that my dog had chronic injuries caused by a trauma, just as I had already attempted to explain to the vet multiple times. No one listened. When the vet called to explain the radiologist report, he was more concerned with insisting that my 11-year old dog see an orthopedic surgeon than listening to my request for a referral to a rehabilitation facility, which I believe is what my dog needs after having cared for him and his chronic injury for 11 years. The vet did not seem to understand that my dog was healthy and happy and does not need surgery at his senior age. The vet initially refused to refer my dog for rehabilitation, insisting that a vet must be present at the rehab facility. This took numerous phone calls and emails from myself and the rehab facility before a referral was provided. When a second referral was requested from a rehabilitation facility facility that could accommodate my dog sooner and was in closer proximity, the vet refused, stating that they could legally not refer a pet to a rehab facility where a vet is not present. I do not know the truth of this statement. This vet has proven to me that they do not listen to critical information provided by pet owners while making diagnoses and they do not have the pet’s best interest in mind. They are more focused on making money by pushing unnecessary testing and medication rather than genuinely helping pets.
Thanks for the fastest and kindest service you gave to my Luna❤️

TL;DR: Brought my dog in late at night for an ear hematoma. TVS confirmed the diagnosis but quoted an absurd $5,000+ for a surgery scheduled two days out, pushed immediate blood tests, and tried adding an undisclosed $85 urgent care fee. Went to my primary vet the next morning, who performed the exact same procedure, testing, and care for $1,625 + tax total. Beware of high-pressure sales and extreme markups here.

I brought my dog to TVS North York Vet Hospital late at night after noticing a hematoma in his ear. Given the late hour and my concern as a pet owner, I called around for costs and decided to visit TVS based on their initial $125 consultation fee.

While the vet quickly confirmed the hematoma diagnosis, everything following the exam was deeply concerning:

1. Exorbitant Surgery Estimate: I was quoted over $4,600 for surgery, plus blood tests and the initial consultation fee, bringing the grand total to over $5,200. To make matters worse, the surgery could not even be performed that night — it was scheduled for two days later. For context, TVS quoted $2,500 for the surgery fee alone and $900 for anesthesia. My regular vet performed the exact same surgery the following day for a $600 surgery fee and $200 for anesthesia.
2. Aggressive Up-selling: The receptionist repeatedly pressured us to do a blood test on the spot. When I explained that $5,000 was a major financial decision and that I wanted to consult my regular vet first, she pushed back, suggesting we run the blood test immediately and "figure it out with insurance later." Passing blood work off to a lab for a procedure scheduled two days out felt entirely driven by securing immediate payment rather than urgent care.
3. Hidden Fees: As we were leaving, an additional $85 "urgent care fee" appeared on our bill without any prior disclosure. I had to challenge this unexpected charge before the receptionist agreed to remove it.

The following morning, I took my dog to my primary vet. They scheduled and performed his surgery promptly for $1,625 + tax total, which covered all necessary pre-op testing, medication, anesthesia, and full post-operative care.

While I expect to pay a premium for extended-hour clinics and urgent care consultations, quoting more than three times the standard rate ($5,200 vs $1,625) alongside high-pressure sales tactics and hidden fees is unacceptable. Please get a second opinion before committing to major procedures here.
